natural_language: The square root of 2 is irrational.
natural_language_proof:
Proof.
If sqrt(2) = a/b in lowest terms, then a^2 = 2b^2 forces both a and b even, contradiction.
lean_code:
import Mathlib.Data.Real.Irrational
import Mathlib.Data.Nat.Prime.Basic
theorem irrational_sqrt_two : Irrational √(2 : ℝ) :=
  irrational_sqrt_two

natural_language: Fundamental theorem of algebra: every non-constant complex polynomial has a root.
natural_language_proof:
Proof.
A nonconstant complex polynomial attains a global minimum of its modulus; a local expansion shows the minimum value must be zero.
lean_code:
import Mathlib.Analysis.Complex.Polynomial.Basic
theorem fundamental_theorem_of_algebra
    {f : Polynomial ℂ} (hf : 0 < f.degree) :
    ∃ z : ℂ, f.IsRoot z :=
  Complex.exists_root hf

natural_language: The rational numbers are denumerable (countably infinite).
natural_language_proof:
Proof.
Q is a quotient of a countable product of countable sets, hence countable; it is infinite, so denumerable.
lean_code:
import Mathlib.Data.Rat.Denumerable
theorem rationals_denumerable : Denumerable ℚ :=
  Rat.instDenumerable

natural_language: Pythagorean theorem: in a right triangle the square of the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides.
natural_language_proof:
Proof.
Right angle means orthogonal legs; expanding the squared hypotenuse via bilinearity yields the sum of squared legs.
lean_code:
import Mathlib.Geometry.Euclidean.Angle.Unoriented.RightAngle
theorem pythagorean_theorem
    {V : Type*} {P : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup V] [InnerProductSpace ℝ V]
    [MetricSpace P] [NormedAddTorsor V P] (p₁ p₂ p₃ : P) :
    dist p₁ p₃ * dist p₁ p₃ = dist p₁ p₂ * dist p₁ p₂ + dist p₃ p₂ * dist p₃ p₂ ↔
      EuclideanGeometry.angle p₁ p₂ p₃ = Real.pi / 2 :=
  EuclideanGeometry.dist_sq_eq_dist_sq_add_dist_sq_iff_angle_eq_pi_div_two p₁ p₂ p₃

natural_language: Law of quadratic reciprocity for distinct odd primes p and q.
natural_language_proof:
Proof.
Compare Legendre symbols via Gauss sums or Eisenstein's lattice-point counting; the sign (-1)^((p-1)(q-1)/4) appears from supplementary laws.
lean_code:
import Mathlib.NumberTheory.LegendreSymbol.QuadraticReciprocity
theorem quadratic_reciprocity
    {p q : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] [Fact q.Prime]
    (hp : p ≠ 2) (hq : q ≠ 2) (hpq : p ≠ q) :
    legendreSym q p * legendreSym p q = (-1) ^ (p / 2 * (q / 2)) :=
  legendreSym.quadratic_reciprocity hp hq hpq

natural_language: Euler's theorem: if x and n are coprime, then x^φ(n) ≡ 1 (mod n).
natural_language_proof:
Proof.
Units modulo n form a group of order phi(n); Lagrange gives x^{phi(n)} ≡ 1 (mod n) when gcd(x,n)=1.
lean_code:
import Mathlib.Data.Nat.Totient
import Mathlib.FieldTheory.Finite.Basic
theorem euler_totient_theorem {x n : ℕ} (h : Nat.Coprime x n) :
    x ^ n.totient ≡ 1 [MOD n] :=
  Nat.ModEq.pow_totient h

natural_language: There are infinitely many prime numbers.
natural_language_proof:
Proof (Euclid).
For any n, n!+1 has a prime factor larger than n.
lean_code:
import Mathlib.Data.Nat.Prime.Infinite
theorem infinitude_of_primes (n : ℕ) : ∃ p : ℕ, n ≤ p ∧ Nat.Prime p :=
  Nat.exists_infinite_primes n

natural_language: Basel problem: the sum of 1/n² over positive integers equals π²/6.
natural_language_proof:
Proof.
Fourier series of x^2 on [-pi, pi], or the Euler product for sine, yields sum 1/n^2 = pi^2/6.
lean_code:
import Mathlib.NumberTheory.ZetaValues
theorem basel_problem :
    HasSum (fun n : ℕ => (1 : ℝ) / n ^ 2) (Real.pi ^ 2 / 6) :=
  hasSum_zeta_two

natural_language: De Moivre's formula: (cos z + i sin z)^n = cos(nz) + i sin(nz).
natural_language_proof:
Proof.
cos z + i sin z = exp(i z); raising to the n-th power gives exp(i n z) = cos(nz) + i sin(nz).
lean_code:
import Mathlib.Analysis.Complex.Trigonometric
theorem de_moivre (n : ℕ) (z : ℂ) :
    (Complex.cos z + Complex.sin z * Complex.I) ^ n =
      Complex.cos (n * z) + Complex.sin (n * z) * Complex.I :=
  Complex.cos_add_sin_mul_I_pow n z

natural_language: Abel–Ruffini: there exists a complex number not solvable by radicals over the rationals (general quintics are not solvable by radicals).
natural_language_proof:
Proof.
An irreducible quintic with Galois group S5 (not solvable) has roots not expressible by radicals.
lean_code:
import Mathlib.FieldTheory.AbelRuffini
-- See also Archive.Wiedijk100Theorems.AbelRuffini
theorem abel_ruffini_exists_not_solvable_by_rad :
    ∃ x : ℂ, ¬ IsSolvableByRad ℚ x :=
  AbelRuffini.exists_not_solvable_by_rad

natural_language: Every natural number is either even or odd.
natural_language_proof:
Proof.
Let n be an arbitrary natural number. By definition of parity, either 2 divides n, or n leaves remainder 1 upon division by 2. In the first case n is even; in the second case n is odd. These cases exhaust all possibilities, so Every natural number is even or odd.
lean_code:
import Mathlib.Data.Nat.Parity
theorem nat_even_or_odd (n : ℕ) : Even n ∨ Odd n :=
  Nat.even_or_odd n

natural_language: The sum of two even natural numbers is even.
natural_language_proof:
Proof.
If m and n are even, write m = 2k and n = 2l. Then m + n = 2(k + l), which is even.
lean_code:
import Mathlib.Data.Nat.Parity
theorem even_add_even {m n : ℕ} (hm : Even m) (hn : Even n) : Even (m + n) :=
  hm.add hn

natural_language: Zero is even.
natural_language_proof:
Proof.
0 = 2 * 0, so 0 is even by definition.
lean_code:
import Mathlib.Data.Nat.Parity
theorem even_zero : Even (0 : ℕ) := Even.zero

natural_language: If n is even then n + 1 is odd.
natural_language_proof:
Proof.
If n = 2k is even, then n + 1 = 2k + 1 is odd.
lean_code:
import Mathlib.Data.Nat.Parity
theorem even_succ_odd {n : ℕ} (h : Even n) : Odd (n + 1) :=
  h.add_one

natural_language: Addition of natural numbers is commutative: m + n = n + m.
natural_language_proof:
Proof.
By induction on m using the recursive definition of addition on the natural numbers.
lean_code: theorem nat_add_comm (m n : ℕ) : m + n = n + m := Nat.add_comm m n

natural_language: Addition of natural numbers is associative.
natural_language_proof:
Proof.
By induction on one summand; both associations satisfy the same recurrence.
lean_code: theorem nat_add_assoc (a b c : ℕ) : a + b + c = a + (b + c) := Nat.add_assoc a b c

natural_language: Multiplication of natural numbers is commutative.
natural_language_proof:
Proof.
By induction, using distributivity and the recursive definition of multiplication.
lean_code: theorem nat_mul_comm (m n : ℕ) : m * n = n * m := Nat.mul_comm m n

natural_language: Multiplication distributes over addition.
natural_language_proof:
Proof.
Fix a and induct on the second summand inside the parentheses.
lean_code: theorem nat_mul_add (a b c : ℕ) : a * (b + c) = a * b + a * c := Nat.mul_add a b c

natural_language: For all natural numbers n, n + 0 = n.
natural_language_proof:
Proof.
Immediate from the definition of addition with second argument zero.
lean_code: theorem nat_add_zero (n : Nat) : n + 0 = n := Nat.add_zero n

natural_language: The successor of a natural number is never zero.
natural_language_proof:
Proof.
Zero is not in the image of the successor function (Peano axioms).
lean_code: theorem nat_succ_ne_zero (n : ℕ) : n.succ ≠ 0 := Nat.succ_ne_zero n

natural_language: ≤ on natural numbers is transitive.
natural_language_proof:
Proof.
If a <= b and b <= c then b = a + k and c = b + l, so c = a + (k + l).
lean_code:
theorem nat_le_trans {a b c : ℕ} (h₁ : a ≤ b) (h₂ : b ≤ c) : a ≤ c :=
  Nat.le_trans h₁ h₂

natural_language: ≤ on natural numbers is reflexive.
natural_language_proof:
Proof.
a = a + 0, hence a <= a.
lean_code: theorem nat_le_refl (a : ℕ) : a ≤ a := Nat.le_refl a

natural_language: From P and P → Q conclude Q (modus ponens).
natural_language_proof:
Proof.
Apply the implication P -> Q to the hypothesis P to obtain Q.
lean_code: theorem modus_ponens {P Q : Prop} (hP : P) (h : P → Q) : Q := h hP

natural_language: P ∧ Q implies Q ∧ P.
natural_language_proof:
Proof.
From P and Q, reassemble as Q and P.
lean_code: theorem and_comm' {P Q : Prop} (h : P ∧ Q) : Q ∧ P := And.symm h

natural_language: If P then P ∨ Q.
natural_language_proof:
Proof.
Use the left introduction rule for disjunction.
lean_code: theorem or_intro_left' {P Q : Prop} (h : P) : P ∨ Q := Or.inl h

natural_language: False implies any proposition.
natural_language_proof:
Proof.
Ex falso quodlibet: from False derive any proposition.
lean_code: theorem false_elim' {P : Prop} (h : False) : P := False.elim h

natural_language: x ∈ A implies x ∈ A ∪ B.
natural_language_proof:
Proof.
Union membership holds if the element is in either set; here it is in A.
lean_code:
import Mathlib.Data.Set.Basic
theorem mem_union_left' {α : Type*} {A B : Set α} {x : α} (h : x ∈ A) :
    x ∈ A ∪ B := Set.mem_union_left B h

natural_language: A ∩ B = B ∩ A.
natural_language_proof:
Proof.
By extensionality: membership in both sides is equivalent to membership in A and in B.
lean_code:
import Mathlib.Data.Set.Basic
theorem inter_comm' {α : Type*} (A B : Set α) : A ∩ B = B ∩ A :=
  Set.inter_comm A B

natural_language: A ∪ B = B ∪ A.
natural_language_proof:
Proof.
Disjunction is commutative, so the unions coincide.
lean_code:
import Mathlib.Data.Set.Basic
theorem union_comm' {α : Type*} (A B : Set α) : A ∪ B = B ∪ A :=
  Set.union_comm A B

natural_language: Subset is reflexive: A ⊆ A.
natural_language_proof:
Proof.
a = a + 0, hence a <= a.
lean_code:
import Mathlib.Data.Set.Basic
theorem subset_refl' {α : Type*} (A : Set α) : A ⊆ A := Set.Subset.refl A

natural_language: (A ∪ B)ᶜ = Aᶜ ∩ Bᶜ (De Morgan).
natural_language_proof:
Proof.
x not in A union B iff x not in A and x not in B iff x in A^c intersect B^c.
lean_code:
import Mathlib.Data.Set.Basic
theorem compl_union' {α : Type*} (A B : Set α) : (A ∪ B)ᶜ = Aᶜ ∩ Bᶜ :=
  Set.compl_union A B

natural_language: (A ∩ B)ᶜ = Aᶜ ∪ Bᶜ (De Morgan).
natural_language_proof:
Proof.
x not in A intersect B iff x not in A or x not in B iff x in A^c union B^c.
lean_code:
import Mathlib.Data.Set.Basic
theorem compl_inter' {α : Type*} (A B : Set α) : (A ∩ B)ᶜ = Aᶜ ∪ Bᶜ :=
  Set.compl_inter A B

natural_language: Length of concatenated lists is the sum of lengths.
natural_language_proof:
Proof.
Induction on the first list: nil contributes 0; cons adds one on both sides.
lean_code:
theorem list_length_append {α : Type*} (l₁ l₂ : List α) :
    (l₁ ++ l₂).length = l₁.length + l₂.length := List.length_append l₁ l₂

natural_language: The empty list has length zero.
natural_language_proof:
Proof.
By the definition of length on the empty list.
lean_code: theorem list_length_nil {α : Type*} : ([] : List α).length = 0 := List.length_nil

natural_language: Absolute value is non-negative: 0 ≤ |x| for x real.
natural_language_proof:
Proof.
Case split on the sign of x; both cases give |x| >= 0.
lean_code:
import Mathlib.Data.Real.Basic
theorem abs_nonneg' (x : ℝ) : 0 ≤ |x| := abs_nonneg x

natural_language: The square of a real number is non-negative.
natural_language_proof:
Proof.
x^2 = |x|^2 >= 0, or case analysis on the sign of x.
lean_code:
import Mathlib.Data.Real.Basic
theorem sq_nonneg' (x : ℝ) : 0 ≤ x ^ 2 := sq_nonneg x

natural_language: |x * y| = |x| * |y| for real numbers.
natural_language_proof:
Proof.
Multiplicativity of absolute value follows by sign cases or from |z|^2 = z^2.
lean_code:
import Mathlib.Data.Real.Basic
theorem abs_mul' (x y : ℝ) : |x * y| = |x| * |y| := abs_mul x y

natural_language: In a group, (a * b)⁻¹ = b⁻¹ * a⁻¹.
natural_language_proof:
Proof.
(b^{-1} * a^{-1}) multiplies with (a * b) to the identity; uniqueness of inverses concludes.
lean_code:
import Mathlib.Algebra.Group.Basic
theorem mul_inv_rev' {G : Type*} [Group G] (a b : G) : (a * b)⁻¹ = b⁻¹ * a⁻¹ :=
  mul_inv_rev a b

natural_language: In a group, (a⁻¹)⁻¹ = a.
natural_language_proof:
Proof.
a is an inverse of a^{-1}; uniqueness of inverses yields the claim.
lean_code:
import Mathlib.Algebra.Group.Basic
theorem inv_inv' {G : Type*} [Group G] (a : G) : (a⁻¹)⁻¹ = a := inv_inv a

natural_language: Composition of continuous functions is continuous.
natural_language_proof:
Proof.
Preimages of opens under g compose with preimages under f to give preimages under g circ f.
lean_code:
import Mathlib.Topology.Basic
theorem continuous_comp' {α β γ : Type*} [TopologicalSpace α]
    [TopologicalSpace β] [TopologicalSpace γ]
    {g : β → γ} {f : α → β} (hg : Continuous g) (hf : Continuous f) :
    Continuous (g ∘ f) := Continuous.comp hg hf

natural_language: gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a % b) for integers (Euclidean algorithm step).
natural_language_proof:
Proof.
Common divisors of a and b coincide with those of b and a mod b.
lean_code:
import Mathlib.Data.Int.gcd
theorem gcd_emod' (a b : ℤ) : Int.gcd a b = Int.gcd b (a % b) := Int.gcd_emod a b

natural_language: Binomial coefficient symmetry: C(n, k) = C(n, n - k).
natural_language_proof:
Proof.
Choosing k elements is equivalent to choosing the complementary n-k elements.
lean_code:
import Mathlib.Data.Nat.Choose.Basic
theorem choose_symm' (n k : ℕ) : n.choose k = n.choose (n - k) :=
  Nat.choose_symm n k

natural_language: Cayley–Hamilton: a matrix annihilates its characteristic polynomial.
natural_language_proof:
Proof.
From the adjugate identity chi(t) I = (tI - A) adj(tI - A), substitute t = A in the polynomial ring to obtain chi(A) = 0.
lean_code:
import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.Charpoly.Basic
theorem cayley_hamilton'
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] {n : Type*} [DecidableEq n] [Fintype n]
    (A : Matrix n n R) : A.charpoly.aeval A = 0 :=
  Matrix.aeval_self_charpoly A

natural_language: A complete metric space is a Baire space.
natural_language_proof:
Proof.
Nested closed balls of vanishing radius inside successive dense opens; completeness yields a point in the intersection.
lean_code:
import Mathlib.Topology.MetricSpace.Baire
theorem complete_metric_baire
    {X : Type*} [MetricSpace X] [CompleteSpace X] [Nonempty X] :
    BaireSpace X := inferInstance

natural_language: Finite separable extensions are simple (primitive element theorem).
natural_language_proof:
Proof.
A finite separable extension has finitely many intermediate fields; a counting argument produces a primitive generator alpha with F(alpha) = E.
lean_code:
import Mathlib.FieldTheory.PrimitiveElement
theorem primitive_element
    {F E : Type*} [Field F] [Field E] [Algebra F E]
    [FiniteDimensional F E] [Algebra.IsSeparable F E] :
    ∃ α : E, F⟮α⟯ = ⊤ :=
  Field.exists_primitive_element F E

natural_language: If R is Noetherian then R[X] is Noetherian (Hilbert basis theorem).
natural_language_proof:
Proof.
Leading-coefficient ideals stabilize by ACC in R; finitely many polynomials realizing those generators generate any ideal of R[X].
lean_code:
import Mathlib.RingTheory.Polynomial.Basic
theorem hilbert_basis {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] :
    IsNoetherianRing R[X] := inferInstance

natural_language: Binomial theorem: (x + y)^n expands as the sum of C(n,k) x^k y^(n-k).
natural_language_proof:
Proof.
Induction on n using Pascal's identity C(n,k)+C(n,k-1)=C(n+1,k).
lean_code:
import Mathlib.Data.Nat.Choose.Sum
theorem binomial_theorem {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R] (x y : R) (n : ℕ) :
    (x + y) ^ n = ∑ m ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), x ^ m * y ^ (n - m) * n.choose m :=
  add_pow x y n

natural_language: Fermat's little theorem: if p is prime and a is not divisible by p, then a^(p-1) ≡ 1 (mod p).
natural_language_proof:
Proof.
(Z/pZ)* has order p-1; a nonzero residue is a unit, so a^{p-1} ≡ 1 (mod p).
lean_code:
import Mathlib.Data.ZMod.Basic
theorem fermat_little {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] (a : ZMod p) (ha : a ≠ 0) :
    a ^ (p - 1) = 1 :=
  ZMod.pow_card_sub_one_eq_one ha

natural_language: Mean value theorem (Cauchy form): there exists c in (a,b) with (g b - g a) f' c = (f b - f a) g' c.
natural_language_proof:
Proof.
Apply Rolle to the auxiliary function that encodes the Cauchy ratio of increments.
lean_code:
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.MeanValue
theorem mean_value_theorem
    {f g : ℝ → ℝ} {a b : ℝ} (hab : a < b)
    (hf : ContinuousOn f (Set.Icc a b)) (hg : ContinuousOn g (Set.Icc a b))
    (hdf : DifferentiableOn ℝ f (Set.Ioo a b))
    (hdg : DifferentiableOn ℝ g (Set.Ioo a b)) :
    ∃ c ∈ Set.Ioo a b,
      (g b - g a) * deriv f c = (f b - f a) * deriv g c :=
  exists_ratio_deriv_eq_ratio_slope hab hf hdf hg hdg

natural_language: Rolle's theorem: if f is continuous on [a,b], differentiable on (a,b), and f(a)=f(b), then some c has f'(c)=0.
natural_language_proof:
Proof.
On a compact interval a continuous function attains an extremum; at an interior extremum the derivative vanishes.
lean_code:
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.MeanValue
theorem rolle
    {f : ℝ → ℝ} {a b : ℝ} (hab : a < b)
    (hfc : ContinuousOn f (Set.Icc a b))
    (hfd : DifferentiableOn ℝ f (Set.Ioo a b))
    (h : f a = f b) :
    ∃ c ∈ Set.Ioo a b, deriv f c = 0 :=
  exists_deriv_eq_zero hab hfc hfd h

natural_language: Intermediate value theorem: a continuous function on [a,b] attains every value between f(a) and f(b).
natural_language_proof:
Proof.
For y between f(a) and f(b), take c = sup{x : f(x) <= y}; continuity forces f(c)=y.
lean_code:
import Mathlib.Topology.Algebra.Order.IntermediateValue
theorem intermediate_value
    {f : ℝ → ℝ} {a b : ℝ} (hab : a ≤ b) (hf : ContinuousOn f (Set.Icc a b)) :
    Set.Icc (f a) (f b) ⊆ f '' Set.Icc a b :=
  intermediate_value_Icc hab hf

natural_language: Chinese remainder theorem: if m,n are coprime then ZMod (m*n) ≃+* ZMod m × ZMod n.
natural_language_proof:
Proof.
The map x |-> (x mod m, x mod n) is a ring isomorphism when gcd(m,n)=1 by comparing cardinalities.
lean_code:
import Mathlib.Data.ZMod.Basic
theorem chinese_remainder {m n : ℕ} (h : Nat.Coprime m n) :
    ZMod (m * n) ≃+* ZMod m × ZMod n :=
  ZMod.chineseRemainder h

natural_language: Bayes' theorem relating conditional probabilities P(t|s) and P(s|t).
natural_language_proof:
Proof.
From P(t|s)=P(s∩t)/P(s) and P(s|t)=P(s∩t)/P(t), eliminate the joint probability.
lean_code:
import Mathlib.Probability.ConditionalProbability
open ProbabilityTheory

    {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω}
    [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    {s t : Set Ω} (hs : MeasurableSet s) (ht : MeasurableSet t) :
    μ[t|s] = (μ s)⁻¹ * μ[s|t] * μ t :=
  cond_prob_eq_inv_mul_cond_prob_mul hs ht

natural_language: Banach fixed-point theorem: a contraction on a complete metric space has a unique fixed point.
natural_language_proof:
Proof.
Iterates of a contraction form a Cauchy sequence; completeness gives a limit fixed by continuity of f; uniqueness follows from K<1.
lean_code:

theorem banach_fixed_point
    {α : Type*} [EMetricSpace α] [CompleteSpace α] [Nonempty α]

    ∃ y, Function.IsFixedPt f y := by
  have : ContractingWith K f := ⟨hf.edist_le_mul⟩
  exact this.exists_fixedPoint

natural_language: Cayley's theorem: every group is isomorphic to a subgroup of a symmetric group.
natural_language_proof:
Proof.
Left multiplication realizes G as a subgroup of the symmetric group on the underlying set of G.
lean_code:

noncomputable def cayley_embedding (G : Type*) [Group G] :

natural_language: Lebesgue decomposition theorem: a measure μ has a Lebesgue decomposition with respect to ν.
natural_language_proof:
Proof.
Any sigma-finite measure splits uniquely into a part absolutely continuous w.r.t. nu and a singular part.
lean_code:

    {α : Type*} [MeasurableSpace α]

  inferInstance

natural_language: Poincaré recurrence theorem: almost every point in a finite-measure invariant set returns infinitely often.
natural_language_proof:
Proof.
If a positive-measure set never returned, the iterates would give infinitely many disjoint positive-measure copies, contradicting finiteness of measure.
lean_code:

    {α : Type*} [MeasurableSpace α] {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure α}
    {f : α → α} {s : Set α}
    (hf : MeasureTheory.MeasurePreserving f μ μ)
    (hs : MeasurableSet s) (hμs : μ s ≠ ⊤) :
    ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, x ∈ s → ∃ᶠ n in Filter.atTop, f^[n] x ∈ s :=
  MeasureTheory.MeasurePreserving.ae_frequently_mem_of_mem_ne_top hf hs hμs

natural_language: Fundamental theorem of algebra (ℂ is algebraically closed).
natural_language_proof:
Proof.
A nonconstant complex polynomial attains a global minimum of its modulus; a local expansion shows the minimum value must be zero.
lean_code:

instance complex_alg_closed : IsAlgClosed ℂ := Complex.isAlgClosed

natural_language: Rational root theorem: any rational root p/q in lowest terms of a polynomial divides accordingly.
natural_language_proof:
Proof.
Clear denominators in p(a/b)=0; unique factorization forces b to divide the leading coefficient and a the constant term.

    {A : Type*} [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [Algebra A ℚ]

natural_language: Lasker–Noether theorem: every submodule of a finitely generated module over a Noetherian ring has a primary decomposition.
natural_language_proof:
Proof.
Noetherian induction produces a primary decomposition; associated primes can be taken distinct.
lean_code:
import Mathlib.RingTheory.Lasker
theorem lasker_noether
    {R M : Type*} [CommSemiring R] [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M]
    {N : Submodule R M} {s : Finset (Submodule R M)}
    (hs : s.inf id = N)
    (hs' : ∀ ⦃J⦄, J ∈ s → J.IsPrimary) :
    ∃ t : Finset (Submodule R M),
      t.inf id = N ∧ (∀ ⦃J⦄, J ∈ t → J.IsPrimary) := by
  obtain ⟨t, ht, ht', _⟩ :=
    Submodule.isPrimary_decomposition_pairwise_ne_radical hs hs'
  exact ⟨t, ht, ht'⟩

natural_language: Rademacher's theorem: a Lipschitz function on R^n is differentiable almost everywhere.
natural_language_proof:
Proof.
Lipschitz maps are absolutely continuous on lines; Fubini reduces a.e. differentiability to the one-dimensional case.
lean_code:
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Rademacher
theorem rademacher
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
    [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
    {F : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F]
    {C : NNReal} {s : Set E} {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure E}
    [MeasureTheory.IsAddHaarMeasure μ]
    {f : E → F} (hf : LipschitzOnWith C f s) (hs : MeasurableSet s) :
    ∀ᵐ x ∂μ.restrict s, DifferentiableWithinAt ℝ f s x :=
  hf.ae_differentiableWithinAt hs

natural_language: Hahn–Banach separation / extension is available in Mathlib for real normed spaces.
natural_language_proof:
Proof.
Extend by Zorn while dominating the functional by a sublinear norm bound.
lean_code:
import Mathlib.Analysis.NormedSpace.HahnBanach.Extension
theorem hahn_banach_norm_extension
    {E : Type*} [SeminormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
    {p : Subspace ℝ E} (f : p →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ) :
    ∃ g : E →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ, (∀ x : p, g x = f x) ∧ ‖g‖ = ‖f‖ :=
  Real.exists_extension_norm_eq p f

natural_language: Open mapping theorem: a surjective continuous linear map between Banach spaces is open.
natural_language_proof:
Proof.
Baire category shows the image of the unit ball is neighborhood of 0; scaling yields openness.
lean_code:
import Mathlib.Analysis.NormedSpace.BoundedLinearMaps
theorem open_mapping
    {E F : Type*}
    [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℂ E] [CompleteSpace E]
    [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℂ F] [CompleteSpace F]
    (f : E →L[ℂ] F) (hf : Function.Surjective f) :
    IsOpenMap f :=
  ContinuousLinearMap.isOpenMap f hf

natural_language: Inverse function theorem (local invertibility of C¹ maps with invertible derivative).
natural_language_proof:
Proof.
A C1 map with invertible derivative is locally invertible by a contraction-mapping argument on a suitable map.
lean_code:
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Inverse
theorem inverse_function_theorem_ref
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [CompleteSpace E]
    {f : E → E} {a : E}
    (hf : ContDiffAt ℝ 1 f a)
    (hf' : ContinuousLinearMap.IsInvertible (fderiv ℝ f a)) :
    ∃ u ∈ nhds a, ∃ g : E → E, ContinuousOn g (f '' u) ∧
      ∀ x ∈ u, g (f x) = x := by
  -- Mathlib: HasStrictFDerivAt.to_localInverse API
  obtain ⟨g, hg⟩ := (hf.contDiffAt.hasStrictFDerivAt).to_localInverse hf'
  exact ⟨_, hg.nhds, g, hg.continuousOn, fun x hx => hg.left_inv hx⟩
